common_name: Ogon Golden Japanese Stonecrop (Chartreuse-Gold Creeping Sedum)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil; Ogon tolerates more shade and moisture than most sedums and roots readily from broken stem pieces.

directions: Ogon is a Japanese selection of Sedum makinoi forming a dense, ground-hugging mat of tiny, rounded, bright chartreuse-gold leaves that turn greener in deep shade and take on warm tones in cool weather. Small, star-shaped yellow flowers appear just above the foliage in summer, though the plant is grown primarily for its glowing foliage color. It performs best in average, well-drained soil with some afternoon shade, which keeps the gold color from scorching while still staying vivid; deeper shade shifts the foliage toward chartreuse-green. Use it to brighten rock gardens, edge pathways, or trail from containers and mixed succulent plantings, and divide congested mats in spring to keep the color fresh.

common_name: Thundercloud Sedum (Gray-Green Dome-Shaped Stonecrop with White Flowers)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Thundercloud forms a tidy, dome-shaped mound and rarely needs staking.

directions: Thundercloud is a patented (USPP 21,833) hybrid stonecrop bred for a compact, low, dome-shaped habit with pointed, gray-green leaves that hold their color well through the growing season. Starry white flower clusters open in late summer above the mounded foliage, a cooler-toned departure from the pink and red shades of most border sedums, and draw bees and butterflies. Grow in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun, where the tight, rounded form stays dense and self-supporting without flopping. It needs only occasional water once established and benefits from being cut back in early spring before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun; Red Cauli's dark stems and densely packed flower heads hold their color best without extra fertility.

directions: Red Cauli is a bushy, mound-forming border stonecrop with dark purple stems and fleshy, purple-flushed, dark blue-green leaves. Its claim to fame is its flower cluster: densely packed, fluffy heads of small pale pink buds open to bright pink and age to deep ruby red, forming a tight, rounded cluster that closely resembles a head of cauliflower. Grow in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun, where the compact habit stays sturdy and self-supporting; the dark seed heads that follow remain rigid through winter for structural interest. This Award of Garden Merit winner combines well with ornamental grasses and other late-season perennials in a border or gravel garden.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Red Carpet spreads into a dense, low mat and roots readily from broken stem pieces.

directions: Red Carpet is a fast-growing, evergreen to semi-evergreen groundcover sedum forming a dense mat of thick, fleshy, medium-green leaves with reddish-tinged margins that deepen to beet-red across fall and winter. Clusters of small, star-shaped, deep reddish-pink flowers open above the foliage in summer, drawing bees and other pollinators. It grows best in average to lean, gritty, well-drained soil in full sun, tolerating drought and poor soil far better than most groundcovers once established. Use it to carpet dry slopes, tuck between paving stones, or edge a rock garden, and trim back any stems that spread beyond their intended area.
